title: Ha Mim again, at the door of a twin surah.
subtitle: A pause before a surah of signs
then: Al-Jathiyah came right after Ad-Dukhan, and the two are so close they read like twins. It opens with the same letters, Ha and Mim. {idea}Their meaning is known to Allah.{/idea} What follows is a surah about the signs all around us.
now: You saw Ha Mim at the start of the last surah too, and your eyes want to slide past. {idea}Treat each opening as a fresh knock at the door.{/idea} Something new is about to be said.
old: I have seen these letters before, so I can skip them.
new: Each time they appear, they ask me to stop and listen again.
try: Before you read this surah, take one slow breath and say bismillah with attention.

title: Sent down from the Mighty, the Wise.
subtitle: Who the Book comes from
then: The surah names its source straight away: the Book is {idea}a revelation from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise{/idea}. The Makkans had doubts about the Quran and about the Hereafter, and this surah answers them.
now: A letter arrives from someone very important and very wise. You would read it slowly, more than once. {idea}This Book's Sender is greater than any of them.{/idea}
old: The Quran is a good book among many.
new: The Quran comes from the Mighty, the Wise, so I read it that way.
try: Read one verse today as if it were a personal letter, and reread it once.

title: The heavens and earth are full of signs for believers.
subtitle: The first step: seeing with faith
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}directs His servants to contemplate His favours and His great power{/idea} in creating the heavens and earth and all kinds of creatures in them. He notes this is the first of three stages: signs for the believers.
now: You take a photo of the sunset for your story and forget it. {idea}The same sky, looked at with faith, is a message.{/idea} The view is the same. The seeing changes.
old: The sky is beautiful, and that is all it is.
new: The sky is a sign, and faith is what lets me read it.
try: Look up at the sky once today and say subhanallah before taking out your phone.

title: Your own body and every creature are signs.
subtitle: The second step: certainty
then: The signs come nearer: {idea}your own creation, and every moving creature spread on the earth{/idea}. Ibn Kathir lists angels, jinn, humans, animals, birds, insects and sea creatures. This time they are signs for {idea}people of certainty{/idea}, a higher stage.
now: You cut your finger and two days later it has healed. You never told it how. A cat stretches on the windowsill. {idea}You are surrounded by signs, and you are one of them.{/idea}
new: My own body is a sign, healing and breathing without my help.
try: Put your hand on your chest for ten seconds today and thank Allah for your heartbeat.

title: Night and day, rain and winds, for those who think.
subtitle: The third step: understanding
then: Ibn Kathir says rain is called {reward}provision{/reward} because it produces all kinds of provision, reviving dry, dead earth. Winds turn north, south, east, west; some bring rain, some pollinate. He notes the verses rise {idea}from believers, to the certain, to those who understand{/idea}.
now: The weather app says rain tomorrow. You groan about the commute. {idea}Somewhere a dry field is waiting for exactly that rain.{/idea} Thinking about it turns a nuisance into a sign.
old: Weather is just something that happens to my plans.
new: Rain and wind are provision being sent, if I think about it.
try: Next time it rains, say the dua for rain or simply thank Allah for it.

title: After Allah's words, what will they believe?
subtitle: If not this, then what
then: Ibn Kathir says the verses {idea}contain the truth from the Truth{/idea}, meaning Allah. So if people do not believe Allah's verses, {trap}what speech after that will they believe in?{/trap}
now: You believe a stranger's video about diet, money and marriage within thirty seconds. You hold the Quran at arm's length. {trap}Notice whose words get your trust fastest.{/trap}
old: I should be sceptical of religious claims but open to others.
new: If I cannot trust His words, no other words deserve more trust.
try: Before you check your feed tomorrow morning, read one verse first.

title: Woe to every sinful liar.
subtitle: A heart shaped by lying
then: Ibn Kathir describes the sinful liar as one {trap}who lies in his speech, often swears{/trap}, and commits and utters sinful acts and words, then disbelieves in Allah's verses. Lying is listed first.
now: "I'm five minutes away" when you have not left. "I swear it was not me." {trap}Each small lie makes the truth a little easier to ignore.{/trap}
old: Little lies are just how everyday life works.
new: A habit of lying makes it harder to hear the truth when it comes.
try: Go one full day without a single small lie, even a polite one.

title: He hears the verses, then acts as if he did not.
subtitle: Hearing without letting it in
then: Ibn Kathir says this person hears the verses recited, {trap}yet persists in his disbelief, denial, pride and rebellion{/trap}, as if he never heard them. The sound reached his ears. Nothing reached his heart.
now: The imam's Friday reminder hits exactly your habit. You nod. By the car park you are back to normal. {trap}As if you had not heard.{/trap}
old: Hearing a reminder counts as taking it in.
new: A reminder I hear and do not act on is one I did not really hear.
try: Take one line from the last talk or reminder you heard and act on it today.

title: He learns a verse and turns it into a joke.
subtitle: Mocking what is sacred
then: Ibn Kathir says if this person {trap}learns anything from the Quran, he takes it as the subject of jest and ridicule{/trap}, and his punishment is humiliating, in return for mocking it. He notes the Prophet ﷺ forbade travelling with the Quran to enemy lands for fear it would be desecrated.
now: A meme in the group chat turns a verse into a punchline. Everyone sends laughing faces. {idea}You do not have to send one too.{/idea}
old: Laughing along with a religious joke is harmless.
new: Allah's words are not material for jokes, even small ones.
try: If you see a joke that mocks a verse, do not share it, and quietly say astaghfirullah.

title: What they earned and their allies will not help.
subtitle: Two kinds of backup that fail
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}their wealth and children will not avail them{/trap}, nor will the false gods they worshipped besides Allah. Everything they built up as protection gives nothing on that Day.
now: You keep a list in your head: the emergency fund, the cousin who is a lawyer, the friend with connections. {idea}All good things, and none of them is your real protector.{/idea}
old: With enough money and the right contacts, I am covered.
new: Money and contacts help here. Only Allah protects in the end.
try: When you check your savings this week, also say: hasbiyallah, Allah is enough for me.

title: This is guidance.
subtitle: Three words that sum up the Quran
then: After describing the liar and the mocker, the verse sums it up. Ibn Kathir says {idea}this is guidance{/idea} refers to the Quran. Those who disbelieve in their Lord's verses face {trap}a painful, severe torment{/trap}.
now: Your map app says: turn left. You can argue with it, but it knows the road. {idea}The Quran is guidance in that plain sense: directions.{/idea}
old: The Quran is mostly about restrictions.
new: The Quran is guidance, directions for getting where I need to go.
try: Read one passage today asking only: what direction is this giving me?
